Pekah
PEE-kuh
proper noun (figure)
Hebrew Peqach (H6492) — "open-eyed" or "watchful," from the same root paqach ("to open the eyes") that produced Pekahiah. The two king-names differ only in the divine-name suffix; the assassin's name dropped it.

📖 Biblical Definition

Pekah (c. 740 — 732 BC) was the eighteenth king of the divided northern kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 15:25-31; 16:5-9; Isaiah 7), captain who assassinated Pekahiah son of Menahem and then aligned with Rezin king of Aram in the great Syro-Ephraimite anti-Assyrian coalition that produced the most theologically loaded crisis of the eighth-century OT. He reigned twenty years in some chronologies (the canonical figure; possibly inflated by including his earlier rebellion-period in Gilead before formally taking Samaria). The Syro-Ephraimite War (c. 734-732 BC) was the campaign in which Pekah of Israel and Rezin of Aram allied to depose Ahaz of Judah and replace him with a puppet ('the son of Tabeel,' Isa 7:6) who would join their anti-Assyrian alliance. Isaiah's confrontation with Ahaz at the conduit of the upper pool (Isa 7:1-25), the Immanuel prophecy, and Ahaz's fateful decision to bribe Tiglath-Pileser III for help against Pekah and Rezin all flow from this crisis. Tiglath-Pileser's response devastated Israel: he annexed Galilee, the Trans-Jordan, and the entire northern third of the kingdom, deporting the populations and reducing Israel to little more than the hill country of Ephraim around Samaria (2 Kings 15:29). The Israelite remnant then assassinated Pekah, and Hoshea son of Elah took the throne as the kingdom's final king. The Assyrian royal annals corroborate the deportation; Tiglath-Pileser claims Pekah's removal as his own action ('they overthrew Peqaha [Pekah] their king, and I placed Auaisi [Hoshea] over them').

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Eighteenth king of Israel (c. 740-732 BC); assassinated Pekahiah; allied with Rezin of Aram in the Syro-Ephraimite War against Ahaz of Judah and Tiglath-Pileser III; the war that triggered Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy (Isa 7:14); Tiglath-Pileser annexed Galilee and Trans-Jordan and deported the populations; assassinated by Hoshea who took the throne.

PEKAH, proper noun. Hebrew Peqach (H6492) — "open-eyed, watchful," from paqach.

Eighteenth king of the divided northern kingdom of Israel (c. 740-732 BC); originally a military captain; assassinated Pekahiah.

Allied with Rezin king of Aram in the Syro-Ephraimite War (c. 734-732 BC) against Ahaz of Judah; the war that occasioned Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy (Isa 7:14).

Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria annexed Galilee, the Trans-Jordan, and the northern third of Israel, deporting the populations (2 Kings 15:29; the first Israelite deportation).

Assassinated by Hoshea son of Elah who succeeded him; attested by name in Tiglath-Pileser's royal annals as 'Peqaha'.

📖 Key Scripture

2 Kings 15:29 — "In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria."

Isaiah 7:4-6 — "Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah. Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against thee, saying, Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the midst of it, even the son of Tabeel."

Isaiah 7:14 — "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

2 Kings 15:30 — "And Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and smote him, and slew him, and reigned in his stead."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Pekah is corrupted when his Syro-Ephraimite coalition is read as merely regional politics rather than as the historical setting that occasioned Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy, when Isaiah's dismissive 'two tails of these smoking firebrands' is read as overconfidence rather than as covenant trust, or when his name's etymology (sharing a root with Pekahiah whom he assassinated) is overlooked.

expand to see more

Syro-Ephraimite War as regional politics. The Pekah-Rezin alliance against Judah and Assyria is often presented in popular treatments as ordinary ancient Near Eastern coalition-building. The narrative's framing in Isaiah 7 makes it the historical setting for one of the most important christological prophecies in the Old Testament. Isaiah confronted Ahaz of Judah with the assurance that 'the two tails of these smoking firebrands' (Pekah and Rezin) would not depose him — if he would trust the LORD. Ahaz refused; Isaiah delivered the Immanuel prophecy anyway. The historical war is theologically inseparable from the Christological promise it occasioned.

Pekah and Pekahiah etymological-irony. The two king-names — Pekahiah (the assassinated) and Pekah (the assassin) — share the root paqach, 'to open the eyes.' The shorter form (Pekah) is the name of the man whose 'open eyes' saw an opportunity to kill his master. The longer Yah-suffixed form (Pekahiah) is the name of the man whose 'open eyes' should have seen Yahweh but did not. The Hebrew text intends this irony; English readers commonly miss it because the spelling-similarity is easier to read past than to read into.

Hebrew Peqach (H6492) — "open-eyed, watchful," from paqach. Eighteenth king of Israel (c. 740-732 BC); assassinated by Hoshea; the Syro-Ephraimite War king.

Hebrew Peqach (H6492) — "open-eyed, watchful"

From the root paqach — "to open the eyes"; same root as Pekahiah

Eighteenth king of the divided northern kingdom of Israel (c. 740-732 BC)

Originally a military captain under Pekahiah; assassinated him with Gileadite forces

Syro-Ephraimite War (c. 734-732 BC) ally of Rezin of Aram; the war occasioned Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy (Isa 7:14)

Tiglath-Pileser III annexed Galilee and Trans-Jordan, deported populations; Pekah assassinated by Hoshea who succeeded him

Usage

"Pekah — the eighteenth king of Israel; assassin of Pekahiah; ally of Rezin in the Syro-Ephraimite War."

"The war that occasioned the Immanuel prophecy of Isaiah 7:14."

"Tiglath-Pileser III's response under his reign was the first Israelite deportation; the kingdom never recovered."
